clue.text: One of many issues want sex put up to let

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: up turns the word put round so that it reads in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants a property advertised to rent, with a saucy phrase thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the middle word round, which works loosely in an across clue. 'Issues' means offspring, not problems or magazines; 'want' and 'to' are padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, and a sextuplet is one of six babies from a single birth, so one of many children.

clue.text: Seeking self esteem of pride before the fall

indicators.note: before places the word for pride ahead of the word for the fall

parts.note: your ego is your pride or self-regard
a trip is a stumble or fall

explanation.surface: A nod to the proverb that pride comes before a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the proverb 'pride goes before a fall', read literally as one word for pride placed before one for a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an action undertaken chiefly to boost one's own vanity, so a quest for self-esteem.

clue.text: Wine spigot holds flysheet in place

definitions.note: a description of what the camping item does, standing for the noun

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine, an old crossword favourite
a spigot is a peg or plug for a cask

explanation.surface: A cask tap seems to be doing duty as a camping fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is a dark red Spanish wine, so 'Wine spigot' looks like a cask tap but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tent peg is driven into the ground to anchor the guy ropes of a tent and its outer sheet.

clue.text: Quality may be correct yet extremely tacky

parts.note: proper means correct or right

indicators.note: extremely means take the letters at the extremes, the first and last, of the word tacky

explanation.surface: A remark that being correct can come across as a bit naff.
explanation.definitionFit: A property is a quality or attribute that something has, as in the properties of a metal.

clue.text: Badly recite for third time

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of recite are to be put in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone fluffs a recitation yet again, on the third attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges RECITE. Tierce, or terce, is the church office said at the third hour of daylight, about 9 a.m.
explanation.definitionFit: Tierce is the canonical hour of prayer said at the third hour after sunrise.

clue.text: Blast urban areas that have short-lived prosperity

definitions.note: a relative clause describing places, standing for the noun

parts.note: a boom is the loud noise of a blast
towns are urban areas

explanation.surface: Explosions hit cities that have enjoyed a brief economic spurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' looks like an exclamation or verb but gives BOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Boomtowns are settlements that grow rapidly with a sudden surge of wealth, often fading again just as fast.

clue.text: Elks can turn on a paw, it is from north America

indicators.note: turn means the word paw is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned
taken as written

explanation.surface: Large deer that can pivot on one foot, native to North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses PAW to WAP, followed by IT IS. 'From north America' adds colour: the wapiti is the North American elk.
explanation.definitionFit: The wapiti is the large North American deer also called the elk.

clue.text: Adaptable flexible relatives

indicators.note: flexible suggests the letters of relatives can be bent into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A family whose members bend to fit any plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' looks like a second definition beside 'Adaptable', but it is the anagram signal for RELATIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatile means able to adapt to many different functions or activities.

clue.text: Historic period of strength ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of puts the word for strength in front of the word for time

parts.note: iron stands for strength, as in an iron will
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A phrase describing an era when strength came before all else.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is the prehistoric era when iron tools and weapons came into wide use.

clue.text: Trust in foreign noble no doubt

parts.note: a count is a nobleman of continental Europe, equivalent to an earl

indicators.note: doubt suggests uncertainty about the order of the letters of no, so they are switched round

explanation.surface: Faith in an aristocrat from abroad, beyond question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubt' rearranges NO into ON. A count is a continental title; Britain has earls instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To count on someone is to rely on or have confidence in them.

clue.text: Stays with the body

definitions.meaning: stays here is a verb: continues to be in a place
a dead person's body is referred to as the deceased's mortal leftovers

explanation.surface: Someone keeps vigil beside a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means continues or lingers; as a noun it is a corpse, the leftover parts of the dead.

clue.text: Let prices tumble-down for orange liqueur

indicators.note: tumble-down suggests a collapse, so the letters of let prices fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A landlord lets rents fall in exchange for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tumble-down' rearranges LET PRICES; it looks like part of a property advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Triple sec is a clear, strong, sweetish liqueur flavoured with orange peel, such as Cointreau.

clue.text: They eat out at work

parts.note: reads like staff having lunch in a restaurant, but describes craftsmen whose acid bites into a metal plate to make a design

explanation.definitionFit: Printmakers of this kind use acid to corrode lines into metal plates as part of their craft.

clue.text: A musician who gets the drift first

indicators.note: first puts the word for the drift at the front, before the suffix for a doer

parts.note: the tenor of a remark is its general drift or gist
the suffix -ist denotes a person who does or gets something

explanation.surface: A player who catches on before everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the drift' is TENOR (its gist), placed first, then -IST, the ending for 'one who'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenorist is a player of a tenor instrument, such as the tenor saxophone.

clue.text: Drunk pig in company of peg

indicators.note: in places the word pig inside the word for a drunk

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy animal keeps company with a wooden pin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like an adjective describing the pig but is SOT, which holds PIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a small wooden plug stopping the vent hole of a cask.

clue.text: She may hold one under her spell

definitions.text: She may hold one under her spell

parts.words: She may hold one under her spell
parts.note: reads like a captivating woman, but literally describes a female practitioner of magic who casts enchantments

explanation.definitionFit: A witch or enchantress casts magic charms, keeping her victims bewitched.

clue.text: So to tune up with range of otic instruments

indicators.note: with here means holding inside, so the word for range goes within the rearranged letters
tune up suggests the letters of so to are adjusted into a new order

parts.note: scope is range or extent

explanation.surface: Instructions for tuning a set of ear instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tune up' rearranges SO TO into OTOS, and 'with' puts SCOPE inside it, before the final S. 'Otic' means relating to the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors use these lighted devices to examine the ear canal and eardrum.

clue.text: Tea can end with wind

parts.note: Typhoo is a well-known British brand of tea

indicators.note: end picks the last letter of the word can

explanation.surface: A drink that leaves the drinker windy.
explanation.walkthrough: Typhoo is a long-established British teabag brand; add N, the end of 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a violent tropical storm of the western Pacific.

clue.text: The gall of the wasp growing in trees

definitions.text: The gall of the wasp growing in trees

parts.words: The gall of the wasp growing in trees
parts.note: gall looks like impudence, but means a round growth that a wasp's larva causes on the twigs of a particular tree

explanation.definitionFit: This spongy round growth forms on oak twigs where a gall wasp has laid its eggs.

clue.text: Dealing and darting about

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of darting are moved around into another order

explanation.surface: Someone does business while dashing around.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading is buying and selling, the business of commerce.

clue.text: Suppose its possible while emus fly back

parts.note: as means while, as in 'as I walked'

indicators.note: fly back means the word emus heads back the other way, reading backwards

explanation.surface: A wistful wonder whether flightless birds might take to the air again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly back' turns the birds round; 'its possible' is surface padding that softens 'Suppose'.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to take something as true without proof.

clue.text: Soothes sun experts

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
aces are experts or top performers

explanation.surface: The best sunbathers say it calms them.
explanation.definitionFit: Solaces comforts or consoles someone in distress.

clue.text: Deck out badly in an off hand way

definitions.text: Deck out badly in an off hand way

parts.words: Deck out badly in an off hand way
parts.note: deck out looks like dressing someone up shabbily, but the deck is a pack of cards handed out wrongly

explanation.definitionFit: A faulty distribution of cards to the players in a game, giving someone the wrong number.

clue.text: Bothers first final of romance with treasures

annotationWithheld.why: Bothers first final of romance with treasures (5,3): CARES (bothers) is clear and 'treasures' defines CARES FOR, but nothing in 'first final of romance' gives FOR; the clue looks garbled and no copy of it was found
annotationWithheld.clue: Bothers first final of romance with treasures

clue.text: Swelling full of fluid in the shoe demand

indicators.note: in says the answer is found within the run of letters of shoe demand

explanation.surface: A blister inside a shoe calls for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'shOE DEMAnd'; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oedema is a build-up of watery fluid in body tissues, causing puffiness.

clue.text: Prove that his stable was in ruins

indicators.note: in ruins suggests the letters of his stable have collapsed into a new order

explanation.surface: Showing that a man's stable has fallen down.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish something is to show it to be true by evidence.

clue.text: Ed first went in back door made of sequoia

indicators.note: in places the leading pieces inside the word turned round
back means the word door is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word went

explanation.surface: Ed was the first through the rear door, made of fine timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the door round to ROOD; the first letter of 'went' follows ED, and the pair goes 'in' after the opening R.
explanation.definitionFit: The sequoia is the giant Californian conifer also called the redwood.

clue.text: Parisian gangsters, cheap as can be

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of cheap as could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: French criminals who come as inexpensive as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as can be' looks like an idiom, but 'can be' is the anagram signal. Apaches were violent Paris street gangsters of around 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: Apache was the name given to violent street ruffians in early twentieth-century Paris.

clue.text: "Starboard" light for ray

parts.note: the sun is our nearest star
a beam is a long piece of timber, like a heavy board

explanation.surface: A ship's right-hand navigation light stands in for a ray.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes around "Starboard" ask you to split the word into its two halves rather than read it as the nautical term; 'light' adds to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunbeam is a shaft of sunlight, a ray from the sky.

clue.text: Harmfully notice poetry lay hollow

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement, a printed notice
verse is poetry

indicators.note: hollow means the inside of the word lay is emptied, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A review damningly calls a poem empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversely means in an unfavourable or damaging way.
